1-Note: No bids will be accepted for this posting, interested parties should contact the undersigned sales representative in order to obtain a Bid package.

2- GCMil requests that bids be submitted electronically to Public Works and Government Services Canada (PWGSC), GCSurplus Contracting Authority by the date, time indicated on page 1 of the bid solicitation package.

*Should you wish to submit paper copies please contact GCSurplus Contracting Authority

3- Brief Summary of the requirement (see Bid package for complete details):

The Department of National Defence has a requirement for the "as and when required" sale of approximately 4,500 MT of scrap, to be sold by the MT (Metric Tonne) per the estimated quantities identified below. The sale is conditional upon the Purchaser demilitarizing or destroying the assets by either cutting, smashing, crushing or smelting to render them unusable/unrepairable or destroyed in accordance with the Controlled Goods Program (CGP), Controlled Technology Access and Transfer (CTAT) and the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR).

The Purchaser and any subcontractor are advised that, within Canada, only persons who are registered, exempt or excluded under the Controlled Goods Program (CGP) are lawfully entitled to examine, possess or transfer controlled goods. Therefore, the successful bidder must be registered under the CGP before a sale contract can be issued. If you are interested in the requirement, please visit the following website to obtain registration details and forms: http://uat-iss-ssi.pwgsctpsgc. gc.ca/dmc-cgd/inscrptn-rgstrtn-eng.html

Note that it takes a minimum of forty five (45) calendar days following submission of all required duly completed documents to the CGP Office, to obtain the certification under the Controlled Goods Program.

The purchaser's facility must be within seventy-five (75) kilometers of the pick-up location, 25 (CFSD) Canadian Forces Supply Depot, 6363 Rue Notre-Dame E Montreal, QC H1N 3V9.

The purchaser must have a 2,000 HP shredder on site capable of processing the various ferrous and non-ferrous metallic assets.

On occasion (as requested) the Purchaser must have equipment, sub-contract or written agreement to enter into a sub-contract with another firm in order to have access to a shredder of a 5,000 HP capacity capable of processing the materials, including iron, of a thickness up to twelve (12) inches to a minimum of one half (1/2) inch which could be contaminated with the following and not limited to: tires, plastic, glass or fabric/textiles, etc.

The purchaser must have a hydraulic shear or a rental agreement for the use of a shear with a jaw pressure of seventy five (75) tons as and when required capable of processing the materials containing in whole or in part ferrous and non-ferrous metal which could be contaminated with the following and not limited to: tires, plastic, glass or fabric/textiles, etc. to a minimum (1/2) inch;

The requirement will be for a period of three (3) years with the option to extend the term of the sale contract by up to two (2) additional one (1) year period(s) under the same conditions. For the first three years of the sale contract: 4,500 MT (estimated quantity)

For the first optional year of the sale contract, if exercised: 1,000 MT (estimated quantity);

For the second optional year of the sale contract, if exercised: 1,000 MT (estimated quantity).

Deposit Required: A five percent (5%) security deposit of the estimated sale contract value will be required from the Purchaser as a condition precedent to Sales Contract award.
